results.section: How the Docs Assistant works (intro)
results.question: Does the Docs Assistant search the internet?
results.answer: No. The Docs Assistant answers only from documents an administrator has uploaded, and it does not search the internet [1]. It also does not use general knowledge to fill gaps [1].

citations.excerpt:
How the Docs Assistant works

The Docs Assistant answers questions using only the documents an administrator has uploaded. It does not search the internet and it does not use general knowledge to fill gaps.

results.section: How the Docs Assistant works › From document to searchable chunks
results.question: What happens if a web page can't be downloaded during indexing?
results.answer: If a web page can't be downloaded during indexing, the worker retries up to four times, with pauses of 2, 4 and 8 seconds between attempts [1]. After the last attempt, the document is marked "failed" and the error is shown in the admin panel [1].

citations.excerpt:
How the Docs Assistant works › From document to searchable chunks

When an administrator uploads Markdown files, PDFs or a web page address, each document is saved with the status "queued" and a background worker picks it up. The worker extracts the text and splits it by section: every heading starts a new chunk of up to about 300 tokens, and each chunk begins with a line naming the document and the section, such as "Ledgerly: account and security › Reset your password". Each chunk is also turned into an embedding, a list of 1536 numbers computed from the words it contains. The chunks are stored in PostgreSQL, with the pgvector extension for the embeddings and a full-text index for the words. When indexing finishes, the document status changes to "ready".

If indexing fails, for example because a web page cannot be downloaded, the worker retries up to four times with growing pauses of 2, 4 and 8 seconds. After the last attempt the document is marked "failed" and the error is shown in the admin panel.

results.question: What do the numbers in square brackets in an answer mean?
results.answer: Each number in square brackets refers to a documentation fragment that the answer is based on. Clicking the number opens the exact text the statement comes from, along with the document, the section and the similarity score. Only fragments that the answer actually cites are shown [2].

results.question: What does the assistant do when the documentation has no answer to a question?
results.answer: If none of the fragments answers the question, the model says that the documentation does not cover it. results.section: Usage limits and privacy › Rate limit
results.question: How many questions can I ask per minute?
results.answer: Each visitor can ask up to 10 questions per minute. If you ask more, the assistant replies with "Too many questions in a short time" and tells you how many seconds to wait [1]. The limit uses a sliding window: as soon as your oldest question is more than a minute old, you can ask again [1].

results.section: Usage limits and privacy › Daily limit
results.question: What is the daily token budget per visitor?
results.answer: Each visitor has a daily budget of 200,000 tokens [1]. There is also a shared daily budget for the whole demo, and budgets reset at 00:00 UTC [1].

citations.excerpt:
Usage limits and privacy › Daily limit

Each visitor has a daily budget of 200,000 tokens. A token is a piece of a word; one question with its answer usually uses between 1,000 and 4,000 tokens, because the documentation fragments are sent along with the question. There is also a shared daily budget for the whole demo. When you reach the daily limit, or the shared budget is used up, the assistant stops answering until 00:00 UTC, when budgets reset.

results.answer: You can ask again at 00:00 UTC, when the budgets reset. Until then, the assistant stops answering once you reach the daily limit or the shared budget is used up [1].

results.section: Usage limits and privacy › What is stored
results.question: Do I need an account to use the chat, and what is stored about me?
results.answer:
No, you do not need an account to use the chat [1].

What is stored about you:
- The browser receives a cookie with a random identifier, which links your conversations and limits together [1].
- Questions and answers are stored in the database so a conversation can be continued after a page reload [1].
- Nothing else about you is collected [1].

citations.excerpt:
Ledgerly: integrations and API › Accounting software

Ledgerly can sync paid invoices to QuickBooks Online and Xero once a day. Connect them in Settings > Integrations. Only invoices with the status Paid are synced, and each invoice is synced once.

Ledgerly: integrations and API › Online payments

Connect Stripe or PayPal in Settings > Payments so clients can pay invoices by card or PayPal. When a payment succeeds, the invoice is marked Paid automatically. Ledgerly does not charge a fee on top of the payment provider's fees.

Ledgerly: integrations and API › Webhooks

Webhooks notify your server when something happens, for example invoice.sent, invoice.viewed and invoice.paid. Add an endpoint URL in Settings > Webhooks. Each request is signed with an HMAC-SHA256 signature in the Ledgerly-Signature header, so you can verify that it came from Ledgerly. Failed deliveries are retried for up to 24 hours.

Ledgerly: integrations and API › API

The Ledgerly REST API is available on the Pro and Team plans. Create an API key in Settings > API keys; the key is shown only once, so store it securely. Send it in the Authorization header as "Bearer" followed by the key.

The API is limited to 60 requests per minute per key. Requests over the limit receive HTTP status 429 with a Retry-After header.
